title: Sherry Trifle
subtitle: Sponge fingers, sherry, custard, and cream in the classic British layers
excerpt: The classic British layered dessert: sherry-soaked sponge fingers, fresh raspberries, a proper egg custard, and softly whipped cream. Make it at least 4 hours ahead.
sourceNotes: A staple of the 20th-century British celebration table. The sherry-soaked sponge layer, set jelly (optional here), egg custard, and whipped cream were codified in cookery books from at least the 1850s.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make at least 4 hours ahead; the trifle keeps covered in the fridge for up to 2 days.

content.text: Sherry trifle is the classic British layered dessert: sherry-soaked sponge fingers, fresh raspberries, a proper egg custard, and softly whipped cream, assembled in a glass bowl so the layers show. The custard is the centrepiece, it needs steady heat and constant stirring to cook through without curdling. Make it at least 4 hours ahead so the custard firms up and the sponge layers absorb the sherry completely.

Spread the sponge fingers with raspberry jam and arrange them in a single layer across the base of a large glass trifle dish. Pour the sherry evenly over the sponge fingers and leave them to soak for 10 minutes. Scatter the raspberries over the top, pressing a few gently into the gaps between the sponge.

Whisk the egg yolks, caster sugar, and cornflour together in a large bowl until pale and smooth. Heat the milk in a medium saucepan over a medium heat until it just begins to steam. Pour the hot milk slowly into the egg mixture, whisking constantly, then return everything to the saucepan. Cook over a low-medium heat, stirring continuously, for 8 to 10 minutes until the custard thickens enough to coat the back of the spoon. Remove from the heat and stir in the vanilla extract. Pour the custard through a sieve directly onto the raspberries and sponge layer. Cover the surface with a disc of cling film to prevent a skin forming and leave to cool to room temperature.
Once the custard is at room temperature, chill the trifle for at least 3 hours. The custard should be set and spoonable when ready.

When the custard has set, whip the double cream with the icing sugar to soft peaks. Spoon or pipe the cream in an even layer over the custard. Return the trifle to the fridge for a further 30 minutes before serving.

items.cause: The heat was too high, or the milk was poured in too fast.
items.fix: Keep the heat at low-medium when cooking the custard and stir constantly. If small lumps appear, pour immediately through a fine sieve.

items.cause: The sherry and fruit have broken down the sponge finger texture.
items.fix: This is expected and correct. If you prefer more texture, reduce the sherry to 60ml.

items.cause: The cream was too warm, or was over-whipped.
items.fix: Chill the bowl and cream before whipping. Stop at soft peaks.

content.text: Best eaten on the day of assembly. Keeps covered in the fridge for up to 2 days.
